core_obligations: Assumption (2) makes $\mathcal{P}$ stable under any base change, giving the direct implication of definition-property-morphisms-local (proof lines 1334-1339).

Set up the converse: fpqc covering $\{Y_i \to Y\}$, $f : X \to Y$ with each $f_i$ having $\mathcal{P}$; by (2) it suffices to show $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ has $\mathcal{P}$ for every affine scheme $Z \to Y$ (proof lines 1339-1349).

Refine: there exists a standard fpqc covering $\{Z_j \to Z\}_{j=1,\ldots,n}$ with morphisms $Z_j \to Y_{i_j}$ over $Y$; each $Z_j \times_Y X \to Z_j$ has $\mathcal{P}$ as a base change of $f_{i_j}$ (proof lines 1349-1356).

Assemble: $Z' = \coprod_j Z_j \to Z$ is surjective flat of affine schemes, so by (1) the coproduct $Z' \times_Y X \to Z'$ has $\mathcal{P}$, and by (3) applied to its base change $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ has $\mathcal{P}$ (proof lines 1356-1365).
proof_roadmap: Derive base-change stability and the direct direction from assumption (2).
Reduce the converse to affine test schemes via assumption (2).
Refine the fpqc covering to a standard affine one mapping into the covering members.
Assemble the coproduct with (1) and conclude with (3).
difficulty_reason: This is the master criterion all fpqc descent lemmas in the chapter feed on. The proof assembles the descent from three assumptions: base-change stability from (2), a reduction to affine test schemes via (2), refinement of the fpqc covering by a standard fpqc covering of affine schemes mapping into the $Y_{i_j}$, a coproduct assembly using (1), and the final application of (3) to the resulting surjective flat morphism of affine schemes.
